message.content: {"answer": "B", "option_text": "The mass is well-circumscribed with an obtuse angle with the chest wall, suggesting an extrapulmonary origin.", "reason": "Figure 1 (lateral chest X-ray) shows a large, dense opacity in the posterior right hemithorax that forms an obtuse angle with the chest wall and has smooth, well-defined margins. These radiographic features are classic signs of an extrapulmonary (pleural or chest wall) mass rather than an intrapulmonary lesion, which typically presents with acute angles and irregular borders. Figures 2 and 3 confirm a large pleural-based mass but are CT scans, not CXRs."}
